text: Golden Disc Awards to make Việt Nam debut in boost for cultural industries

HÀ NỘI - The 41st Golden Disc Awards will be held in Hà Nội for the first time in January 2027, bringing one of South Korea's biggest music events to Việt Nam and opening up opportunities to promote the country's cultural industries and tourism.

The announcement was made at a press conference on November 11 by the Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism and Military Commercial Joint Stock Bank (MB), marking the launch of their cooperation programme, "Việt Nam - Experience More", for the 2027-31 period.
The 41st Golden Disc Awards (GDA 41) is scheduled to take place on January 9-10, 2027, at the Việt Nam Exhibition Centre (VEC) in Hà Nội.
Organisers expect around 70,000 audience visits over the two nights, including an estimated 35,000 international visitors.
Established in 1986, the Golden Disc Awards is one of South Korea's longest-running and most prestigious music awards.

It recognises outstanding achievements in the music industry, covering both album sales and digital music releases, and has accompanied the growth of Korean popular music and the global expansion of K-pop.

Having previously been hosted in major Asian cities such as Tokyo, Taipei and Hong Kong, the awards will come to Việt Nam for the first time, giving Hà Nội an opportunity to host an internationally recognised music event and strengthen cultural and creative exchanges between Việt Nam and South Korea.

Kim Yu-seok, a representative of HLL JoongAng, which manages the Golden Disc Awards' intellectual property rights, said the awards had evolved from a domestic music ceremony into an event eagerly anticipated by K-pop fans worldwide.

Hosting the ceremony in Hà Nội would offer more than performances by leading South Korean artists, he said, creating opportunities for exchanges and cooperation between the two countries' entertainment industries.
The ceremony will be broadcast in South Korea and other Asian markets, bringing the Hà Nội stage to international audiences.

Kim expressed hope that the event would also help position Hà Nội as an emerging destination for major Asian music festivals and mark a new milestone in Việt Nam-South Korea entertainment industry cooperation.

The 40th Golden Disc Awards, held in Taipei, Taiwan (China), attracted around 290 million global views, nearly 50 million votes and close to 80,000 in-person spectators, with international ticket buyers accounting for almost half of the audience, according to figures released at the press conference.
The figures highlight the international reach of major music events and their potential to generate demand for tourism, hospitality, retail and other services.
Under the Việt Nam - Experience More programme, the organisers plan to develop a broader experience ecosystem for fans and visitors before, during and after the awards.
The proposed package will connect event tickets with flights, accommodation, dining, shopping, heritage visits and cultural experiences.
It is also intended to encourage international visitors to extend their stays in Hà Nội and explore nearby destinations, including Hạ Long, Ninh Bình and Hà Giang.

Destination promotion, along with content showcasing Việt Nam's culture and people, is also being considered for integration into a dedicated information hub for the event, providing additional material for international communications.
Technology and digital engagement will form another part of the programme.

MB plans to develop a dedicated Golden Disc Awards experience on its MBBank mobile banking application, allowing users to personalise the interface around their favourite artists and take part in interactive activities and voting.
A fan voting campaign in Việt Nam will also give local audiences the opportunity to select their favourite K-pop artist, who will receive a special award on the Golden Disc Awards stage.

Meanwhile, music experiences and cultural exchange activities between Việt Nam and South Korea are expected to take place in public spaces, bringing the atmosphere of the awards closer to local audiences and creating more opportunities for public participation.
The combination of live events, international communications and digital services reflects a broader approach to expanding cultural experiences through technology.
If effectively implemented, it could also help develop audiences, generate new service products and strengthen the value chains of the cultural and creative industries.
Turning events into economic opportunities
The decision to bring the 41st Golden Disc Awards to Hà Nội offers Việt Nam an opportunity to raise its international profile and deepen cultural exchanges.
However, the broader ambition of the Việt Nam - Experience More programme is to turn the appeal of major events into a driver of growth across multiple sectors.

Through the Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism's policy direction, businesses' involvement and cooperation with international partners, the programme seeks to go beyond bringing high-profile events to Việt Nam.
It aims to create an environment in which cultural assets can be developed into marketable products, services and new sources of economic value.

In this approach, a major event is not simply an entertainment attraction but can become part of a wider value chain connecting cultural industries, tourism and the sports economy, while promoting Việt Nam as a destination offering diverse and distinctive experiences. - VNS
